description: A query performance budget defines concrete, enforceable latency and timeout limits per workload class, ensuring database behavior stays within API SLO requirements.

rules.description: The spec must declare workloads (object with at least one class) and max_transaction_duration.
Each workload class must declare statement_timeout as a concrete duration string (5s, 500ms, 2m). Vague values (high, acceptable, tbd) are rejected — they cannot be enforced by PostgreSQL.
max_transaction_duration must be a finite, concrete duration. unlimited or infinite are rejected. Long transactions hold locks, prevent autovacuum, and cause replication lag.
Workloads with is_replica: true must have statement_timeout <= the primary write workload timeout. Looser replica timeouts can cause hot standby conflicts and replication lag.
When api_slo_ms is declared, each workload's p99_latency_ms must be <= api_slo_ms * 0.7. The database budget must leave headroom for the application layer.
Every timeout field (statement_timeout, lock_timeout, idle_in_transaction_timeout) must be a parseable duration string. Vague strings cannot be converted to PostgreSQL GUC parameters.
